name: Tropical Urban Green Space Clips: Restorativeness by Sight and Sound
description:
Replication of the Malaysian tropical urban green space study by Hoo, Sidhu & Tan, built from their Tropical Environmental Stimuli Database (TESD; Research Square preprint, doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11534093/v1) and the open codebook and data of the main rating study "Sensing nature in the city: The role of sight and sound in restorative tropical urban green spaces" (OSF osf.io/4cbyq, manuscript submitted). Each participant is assigned at random to one of three groups: sound only, picture only (muted video), or picture and sound. They then experience 30 clips drawn at random from the 120 TESD stimuli (50 nature, 20 mixed urban-nature and 50 urban scenes, each 5 seconds long), in random order. After each clip they rate naturalness (0 = not natural at all, 10 = cannot be more natural) and five restorative qualities, fascination, being away, coherence, scope and compatibility, each from 0 to 10. Analysis as in the open data: perceived restorativeness (PRS) = mean of the five items; compare environment type and sensory group. In the open data (87 participants, Feb–Apr 2024), nature and mixed scenes were rated more restorative than urban scenes in every group, and nature scenes scored highest when people could both see and hear them.

Stimuli: TESD post-refinement set from OSF osf.io/whced (CC BY-NC 4.0), re-encoded to 640 px wide H.264 with AAC audio so the set fits the platform; used with credit for non-commercial research; the template is removed if the authors object.

Differences from the original study: (1) the restorativeness items are our own one-line statements, one per dimension; the original used the Perceived Restorativeness Scale – Short Form (and a soundscape-adapted version for the sound-only group), whose wording is not given in the open materials; (2) here the five 0–10 items are tap buttons; in the original, naturalness used a continuous 0–10 slider; (3) the sound-only group plays the clip's soundtrack with the picture hidden, rather than separate audio files; (4) participants must play each clip once before rating and may replay it; (5) the clips are lower resolution than the 1920 × 1080 originals; (6) an online consent checkbox and an optional headphones/speakers question were added; demographic questions are not included because the open materials do not list them. The underlying papers were not yet peer-reviewed when this template was made (preprint and submitted manuscript).

elements.title: Rate this place.
elements.description: 30 clips drawn at random from the 120 TESD stimuli (key = file name: N_001 … N_050 nature, HUHN_001 … HUHN_020 mixed urban-nature, U_001 … U_050 urban), in random order. Value: {naturalness, fascination, being_away, coherence, scope, compatibility}, each 0–10. PRS = mean of the five restorativeness items. Analysis as in the open data: compare environment (nature / mixed / urban) and modality (audio / visual / bimodal) with mixed models on PRS and naturalness.
